Preserve the request's range/conditional headers, use `context.signal` for cancellation and return a streaming response. Document which HTTP features your source supports.

If you implement `redirect(asset)`, validate the public destination before returning it. Validate every redirect in `open()` too, and don't forward credentials to another host. Without `redirect()`, Upserve uses `open()` even for public assets.

For private data, set `private: true`; registration will then require `authorize()` and downloads will stream through the server. Change the nonsecret `scope` whenever the source configuration or credential permissions change.

## Common mistakes

- Returning `[]` during an outage withdraws every release. Throw instead.
- Using client input as an upstream URL turns the server into a proxy. Resolve assets from your trusted catalog.
- Caching malformed source responses inside `context.cached()` can preserve bad data. Validate before returning.
- Treating `scope` as a token risks storing secrets in keys. Use a credential generation name.

The [Provider and ResourceContext reference](/docs/api#provider) covers the optional webhook hook and exact signatures. Add tests for malformed data, denied access, ranges, redirects and cancellation before using a network-backed provider for executable downloads.


---
title: Custom adapters
description: Add and test a small update protocol while reusing release resolution and caching.
---

An adapter defines the routes and responses your updater expects. Use one when the generic API doesn't fit your client. It can work with GitHub or any custom provider without knowing where the releases came from.

Upserve supplies application-scoped release lookup, manifest loading and asset delivery. Your adapter validates its protocol and decides what response represents an applicable update.

## 1. Define a route

Install `@neplex/upserve`. This adapter returns a small version response at `/editor/stable/custom/version`:

```ts title="version-adapter.ts"
import { defineAdapter } from "@neplex/upserve";

export function versionAdapter() {
  return defineAdapter({
    name: "custom-version",

    register(router, services) {
      router.get("/custom/version", async (context) => {
        const channel = context.req.param("channel")!;
        const release = await services.latest(channel);

        if (!release) return context.body(null, 204);

        return context.json({ version: release.version, notes: release.notes });
      });
    },
  });
}
```

Routes are relative to `/:application/:channel`. The outer router supplies `channel`, checks application access and adds metadata caching headers and ETags. Choose a path prefix that doesn't collide with another adapter.

## 2. Register it

Put `versionAdapter()` in your application's `adapters` array. It can sit beside `tauri()` or `generic()` if their paths don't overlap. The adapter name must also be unique within that application.

## 3. Test the public endpoint

Use `catalog-provider.ts` from the [provider guide](/docs/custom-providers). Install `vitest` as a development dependency, save all three files together and run `npx vitest run version-adapter.test.ts`:

```ts title="version-adapter.test.ts"
import { expect, it } from "vitest";
import { createUpserve } from "@neplex/upserve";
import { catalogProvider } from "./catalog-provider.js";
import { versionAdapter } from "./version-adapter.js";

it("answers in the custom protocol", async () => {
  const updates = createUpserve({
    apps: {
      editor: { provider: catalogProvider(), adapters: [versionAdapter()] },
    },
  });

  const response = await updates.request("/editor/stable/custom/version");

  expect(response.status).toBe(200);
  expect(await response.json()).toEqual({
    version: "1.2.0",
    notes: "Fixes startup on older systems.",
  });
});
```

No live source or HTTP listener is needed for this test.

## 4. Add manifests and downloads

Use `services.releases(channel)` when you need the full ordered history. Use `services.manifest(release, "update.json", parse)` to read a **known asset** and validate it before it is cached. The parser receives text, must throw on invalid protocol data, and runs again on cache hits.

Check the manifest version, required platforms, signatures and referenced assets before returning an offer. A valid release list alone doesn't mean a protocol manifest is complete. Don't alter cryptographic signatures or checksums.

For a download URL in JSON, call `services.assetUrl(context, release, asset)`. For a download route of your own, return `services.deliver(context.req.raw, release, asset)`. That service applies configured redirects or streaming, including private delivery. Use `GET` and `HEAD` routes if your protocol needs both.

## Common mistakes

Don't call GitHub directly from each route. Use the supplied services so your protocol shares caching and refresh coordination. Don't add a client-controlled force-refresh option or expose another application's configuration.

Return `204` when your protocol has no applicable update. Throw an `UpserveError` for invalid data rather than presenting an incomplete release. Add tests for unsupported platforms, current versions, missing assets, authentication and mounted paths before shipping.

See [AdapterServices](/docs/api#adapterservices) for method signatures and [error responses](/docs/errors) for the default error mapping.


---
title: Custom cache stores
description: Implement metadata storage without reimplementing cache timing or refresh coordination.
---

A cache store saves entries. Upserve decides when they're fresh, when to refresh and whether stale data can still be used. You don't need to implement those policies in your store.

Use the built-in memory or SQLite store unless you have another storage requirement. A shared store can make metadata available to several processes, but it doesn't coordinate their upstream requests.

## 1. Implement the three methods

Install `@neplex/upserve`. This complete example adds a write counter to a small in-memory store so you can see how the contract works. It isn't bounded; use `memoryCache()` for normal deployments.

```ts title="counted-cache.ts"
import { defineCache } from "@neplex/upserve";
import type { CacheEntry } from "@neplex/upserve";

export function countedCache() {
  const entries = new Map<string, CacheEntry>();

  let writes = 0;

  return defineCache({
    async get(key: string) {
      const entry = entries.get(key);

      return entry === undefined ? undefined : structuredClone(entry);
    },

    async set(key: string, entry: CacheEntry) {
      entries.set(key, structuredClone(entry));
      writes++;
    },

    async delete(key: string) {
      entries.delete(key);
    },

    stats() {
      return { writes };
    },
  });
}
```

`defineCache()` preserves `stats()` on the returned object, but Upserve only calls `get`, `set` and `delete`.

## 2. Register it

Pass `cache: countedCache()` at the top level of `createUpserve()` or `defineConfig()`. Keep per-application lifetimes in `apps.editor.cache`. See [applications](/docs/configuration) for that distinction.

## 3. Test storage behavior

Install `vitest` as a development dependency, save this next to the implementation and run `npx vitest run counted-cache.test.ts`:

```ts title="counted-cache.test.ts"
import { expect, it } from "vitest";
import { countedCache } from "./counted-cache.js";

it("isolates values and preserves absolute timestamps", async () => {
  const cache = countedCache();
  const entry = {
    value: { version: "1.2.0" },
    freshUntil: 60_000,
    staleUntil: 360_000,
    retryAt: 30_000,
  };

  await cache.set("editor", entry);
  entry.freshUntil = 0;

  expect(await cache.get("editor")).toEqual({
    value: { version: "1.2.0" },
    freshUntil: 60_000,
    staleUntil: 360_000,
    retryAt: 30_000,
  });

  await cache.delete("editor");

  expect(await cache.get("editor")).toBeUndefined();
  expect(cache.stats()).toEqual({ writes: 1 });
});
```

For a persistent implementation, add a test that closes and reopens the store before reading the entry.

## 4. Adapt it to persistent storage

Use the full key unchanged, make each write atomic and return independent values so callers can't mutate stored data. Preserve `freshUntil`, `staleUntil` and `retryAt` as **absolute epoch milliseconds**, not durations.

Don't delete an entry just because `freshUntil` has passed. Upserve may still use it during the stale window or use its validators for refresh. An entry with `value: undefined` can record a failure cooldown; preserve its timestamps too. JSON drops `undefined` object properties, so decoding a missing `value` as `undefined` must remain valid.

Persistent caches can contain private release metadata. Restrict access, choose namespaces deliberately and plan retention for obsolete keys. Your store's lifecycle and cleanup methods are yours to manage; `CacheStore` has no close or prune hook.

## Common mistakes

A shared database isn't a distributed lock. Multiple Upserve processes can refresh simultaneously even when they read the same entries. Don't advertise global concurrency or rate-limit guarantees unless you implement and validate an additional coordination system yourself.

Keep installer bytes out of metadata entries. Reject or surface storage failures rather than silently pretending that a write succeeded. See the [cache contract](/docs/api#cachestore-and-cacheentry) and [cache behavior](/docs/cache) for the full semantics.


---
title: Public API
description: Find exported functions, integration options and extension contract semantics.
---

All core imports below come from `@neplex/upserve`. Providers, adapters and SQLite are separate packages so you only install what you use. Runtime configuration fields are listed in the [configuration reference](/docs/configuration-reference).

## createUpserve

`createUpserve(config: UpserveConfig): Upserve`

Creates a real Hono application with `.fetch`, `.request`, `.route` and the normal Hono methods. It doesn't start a listener. Use the [quick start](/docs/quick-start) for a complete Node.js example or [embedding](/docs/embedding) to mount it.

`Upserve` adds two trusted server-side methods:

| Method                                           | What it does                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `refresh(application: string): Promise<void>`    | Forces release-list and provider-resource revalidation, respecting failure cooldowns |
| `invalidate(application: string): Promise<void>` | Waits for the pending list load, then deletes the resolved release-list entry        |

Both reject unknown application IDs with `UpserveError("missing", ...)`. Neither is an HTTP administration endpoint. Refresh doesn't clear all adapter manifests; see [cache refresh behavior](/docs/cache#make-new-releases-available).

## defineConfig, defineProvider, defineAdapter and defineCache

Each helper accepts an object satisfying its public contract and returns the same object with its inferred type. Use them for autocomplete and to catch missing methods without implementing a base class.

| Helper                     | Contract        | Example                                    |
| -------------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `defineConfig(config)`     | `UpserveConfig` | [Configuration](/docs/configuration)       |
| `defineProvider(provider)` | `Provider`      | [Catalog provider](/docs/custom-providers) |
| `defineAdapter(adapter)`   | `Adapter`       | [Version adapter](/docs/custom-adapters)   |
| `defineCache(cache)`       | `CacheStore`    | [Counted cache](/docs/custom-cache-stores) |

They don't perform extra runtime wrapping or sandbox plugin code.

## memoryCache

`memoryCache(maxEntries = 1000): CacheStore`

Creates a process-local least-recently-used store. `maxEntries` must be a positive integer. Reads and writes clone values so callers can't mutate stored entries. The limit counts metadata entries, not bytes. Restarting the process loses the data.

## sqliteCache

Import `sqliteCache` from `@neplex/upserve-sqlite`.

`sqliteCache(filename: string): CacheStore & { close(): void }`

Opens a Node SQLite metadata database in WAL mode. Create its parent directory first and close it after HTTP work drains. Entries survive restarts; old rows aren't automatically pruned. See the [persistent cache example](/docs/cache#persist-metadata-with-sqlite).

## Version helpers

| Function                                             | Result                                                                                                               |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `validVersion(version: string): boolean`             | Tests a semantic version without coercing an arbitrary tag                                                           |
| `newer(candidate: string, current: string): boolean` | Returns whether the candidate has greater semantic-version precedence; throws `invalid` if either version is invalid |
| `compareVersions(a: string, b: string): number`      | Descending sort comparator for semantic versions; pass valid versions                                                |

```ts title="versions.ts"
import { compareVersions, newer, validVersion } from "@neplex/upserve";

validVersion("1.2.0"); // true
newer("1.2.0", "1.1.0"); // true

const versions = ["1.9.0", "1.10.0"].sort(compareVersions);

console.log(versions); // ["1.10.0", "1.9.0"]
```

Build metadata doesn't change precedence. Tags and provider IDs shouldn't be passed as versions.

## readText

`readText(response: Response, maxBytes = 1024 * 1024): Promise<string>`

Reads UTF-8 metadata up to a byte limit, cancels on overflow and releases its stream reader. It returns an empty string when there's no body. Use it before parsing untrusted metadata; don't use it for installers.

## UpserveError

`new UpserveError(code, message, retryAt?)`

| Property  | Type                                                                                 | Meaning                                                                      |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `code`    | `"configuration"`, `"auth"`, `"rate_limit"`, `"network"`, `"invalid"` or `"missing"` | Failure category                                                             |
| `message` | `string`                                                                             | Safe operational explanation; don't include credentials or raw source bodies |
| `retryAt` | `number` (optional)                                                                  | Earliest refresh time as absolute epoch milliseconds                         |

An `auth` error clears the affected cached entry. Other failures can preserve previously validated data within its stale window. See [HTTP errors](/docs/errors) for the client mapping.

## Integration factories

### GitHubOptions

`github(options: GitHubOptions): Provider` from `@neplex/upserve-github`.

The [GitHub guide](/docs/github#options-you-may-need) lists all deployment options, requirements and defaults. These additional options support deterministic testing:

| Option   | Type                            | Required | Default           | Purpose                                             |
| -------- | ------------------------------- | -------- | ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `fetch`  | `typeof fetch`                  | No       | Global `fetch`    | Supply recorded API responses without real requests |
| `sleep`  | `(ms: number) => Promise<void>` | No       | Timer-based delay | Control retry backoff                               |
| `random` | `() => number`                  | No       | `Math.random`     | Supply jitter from zero to one                      |

### TauriOptions

`tauri(options?: TauriOptions): Adapter` from `@neplex/upserve-tauri`.

| Option     | Type     | Required | Default         | Meaning                                     |
| ---------- | -------- | -------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `manifest` | `string` | No       | `"latest.json"` | Manifest asset name in the selected release |

See [Tauri](/docs/tauri) for endpoint and manifest requirements.

### ElectronOptions

`electron(options?: ElectronOptions): Adapter` from `@neplex/upserve-electron`.

| Option     | Type                     | Required | Default                                          | Meaning                                     |
| ---------- | ------------------------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------- |
| `channels` | `Record<string, string>` | No       | `stable` maps to `latest`; others use their name | Maps URL channels to YAML filename prefixes |

For example, `electron({ channels: { prerelease: "beta" } })` serves `beta.yml` on the `prerelease` channel. This doesn't replace application channel predicates. See [Electron](/docs/electron).

### AndroidOptions

`android(options?: AndroidOptions): Adapter` from `@neplex/upserve-android`.

| Option       | Type                                                       | Required | Default                    | Meaning                                         |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `manifest`   | `string`                                                   | No       | `"latest-android.json"`    | Manifest asset name                             |
| `transform`  | `(input: unknown) => AndroidManifest`                      | No       | Use parsed input           | Translates another format before validation     |
| `compatible` | `(manifest: AndroidManifest, request: Request) => boolean` | No       | No extra eligibility check | Returning false suppresses the offer with `204` |

`AndroidManifest` is also exported by this package. Its fields and validation rules are in the [Android manifest reference](/docs/android#manifest-fields). `minimumVersion` and `versionCode` aren't automatic selection rules.

### generic

`generic(): Adapter` from `@neplex/upserve-generic` takes no options. Its response format is documented in [custom applications](/docs/generic).

## Extension contracts

The following types are exported from the core. Official integrations implement these same contracts.

### Release and Asset

| Release field     | Type      | Required | Meaning                                                                  |
| ----------------- | --------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `id`              | `string`  | Yes      | Stable provider identity                                                 |
| `tag`             | `string`  | Yes      | Original upstream reference                                              |
| `version`         | `string`  | Yes      | Valid semantic version                                                   |
| `prerelease`      | `boolean` | Yes      | Channel-selection flag                                                   |
| `assets`          | `Asset[]` | Yes      | Known manifests and downloadable files, up to 1,000                      |
| `draft`, `yanked` | `boolean` | No       | Exclude the release when true                                            |
| `notes`           | `string`  | No       | Release notes                                                            |
| `publishedAt`     | `string`  | No       | RFC 3339 timestamp                                                       |
| `metadata`        | `unknown` | No       | Serializable source-specific information; omitted from generic responses |

An `Asset` has required `id: string`, `name: string`, `size: number` and `url: string`, plus optional `contentType: string`. Size is a nonnegative integer in bytes. IDs and names must each be unique within a release. Providers must validate URLs for their delivery policy; the core's URL-shape check isn't a source-specific security policy.

The core accepts at most 10,000 releases, filters drafts/yanked entries and sorts by version. Adapter manifests have additional validation requirements.

### Provider

| Member          | Signature                                                                         | Responsibility                                                  |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`          | `string`                                                                          | Identify the integration                                        |
| `scope`         | `string`                                                                          | Identify a nonsecret configuration/credential generation        |
| `private`       | `boolean` (optional)                                                              | Require authorization and streamed downloads when true          |
| `releases`      | `(context: ResourceContext) => Promise<Release[]>`                                | Return validated source data or throw                           |
| `open`          | `(asset: Asset, request: Request, context: ResourceContext) => Promise<Response>` | Open only the known asset and preserve supported HTTP semantics |
| `redirect`      | `(asset: Asset) => string` (optional)                                             | Return a validated public download destination                  |
| `verifyWebhook` | `(request: Request, body: Uint8Array) => Promise<boolean>` (optional)             | Authenticate a bounded webhook body before refresh              |

A provider with `verifyWebhook` gets `/webhooks/:application`. The official GitHub provider exposes that method even without a secret; verification then rejects every delivery. See the [provider tutorial](/docs/custom-providers) for implementation and testing.

### ResourceContext

| Member   | Signature                                                                             | Meaning                                                               |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `signal` | `AbortSignal`                                                                         | Cancellation/deadline for the operation                               |
| `cached` | `<T>(identity: string, load: (previous: T \| undefined) => Promise<T>) => Promise<T>` | Cache and coalesce a resource inside the application's provider scope |

Validate inside `load` before returning. Provider resources have no stale-on-error fallback of their own; the outer release list can still supply stale data. Release lookup gets a 120-second outer deadline; adapter manifest loading gets 30 seconds. Providers should honor the signal and bound their own requests too.

### Adapter

`Adapter` requires `name: string` and `register(app: Hono, services: AdapterServices): void`. Register relative routes under the application's channel router. Names and route prefixes should avoid collisions. See the [adapter tutorial](/docs/custom-adapters).

### AdapterServices

| Member     | Signature                                                                       | Meaning                                                           |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `config`   | `AppConfig`                                                                     | This application's configuration                                  |
| `channels` | `string[]`                                                                      | Configured channel names                                          |
| `releases` | `(channel: string) => Promise<Release[]>`                                       | Filtered releases, newest first                                   |
| `latest`   | `(channel: string) => Promise<Release \| undefined>`                            | First selected release                                            |
| `manifest` | `<T>(release: Release, name: string, parse: (text: string) => T) => Promise<T>` | Read a known asset, validate before caching and parse on each use |
| `assetUrl` | `(context: Context, release: Release, asset: Asset) => string`                  | Build a server delivery URL including a parent mount path         |
| `deliver`  | `(request: Request, release: Release, asset: Asset) => Promise<Response>`       | Apply redirects or streaming to a known release asset             |

`Context` is Hono's request context. Manifest bodies are limited to 1 MiB through `readText()` by default. A parse failure becomes an `invalid` error and doesn't replace previously validated text. Don't return invalid data from the parser.

### CacheStore and CacheEntry

| CacheStore method                     | Return type                        | Meaning                                 |
| ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `get(key: string)`                    | `Promise<CacheEntry \| undefined>` | Return an independent entry or no entry |
| `set(key: string, entry: CacheEntry)` | `Promise<void>`                    | Atomically save the complete entry      |
| `delete(key: string)`                 | `Promise<void>`                    | Remove that exact key                   |

`CacheEntry` contains `value: unknown`, `freshUntil: number`, `staleUntil: number` and optional `retryAt: number`. Timestamps are absolute epoch milliseconds. An undefined value can record a failed cold load and its cooldown. Preserve it rather than interpreting it as fresh empty data.

`CachePolicy`, `AppConfig` and `UpserveConfig` are documented in [configuration options](/docs/configuration-reference). See the [cache tutorial](/docs/custom-cache-stores) for storage semantics and restart tests. The internal coordinator and validation schemas aren't public exports.


---
title: Configuration options
description: Look up required fields, defaults and advanced server settings.
---

Use this reference after the [quick start](/docs/quick-start). Configuration uses the same `UpserveConfig` shape for `createUpserve()` and the CLI's `defineConfig()`.

## UpserveConfig

| Option        | Type                               | Required | Default             | Behavior                                                                  |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------- | -------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `apps`        | `Record<string, AppConfig>`        | Yes      | None                | Registers applications by URL identifier                                  |
| `cache`       | `CacheStore`                       | No       | `memoryCache(1000)` | Chooses the metadata store shared by this instance                        |
| `namespace`   | `string`                           | No       | `"upserve-v1"`      | Separates deployment data in the store                                    |
| `concurrency` | `number`                           | No       | `4`                 | Limits simultaneous loads per coordination pool; integer `1` through `64` |
| `now`         | `() => number`                     | No       | `Date.now`          | Supplies epoch milliseconds for cache timing in deterministic tests       |
| `background`  | `(task: Promise<unknown>) => void` | No       | None; await refresh | Lets the host keep a stale-data refresh alive after responding            |

Use `namespace` when multiple deployments share a persistent store. Change it when you change a deployment's security boundary. It isn't a secret.

There are separate coordination pools for resolved metadata and provider resources. `concurrency` doesn't limit active binary downloads or enforce a distributed budget. `now` controls cache timing; it doesn't replace GitHub's wall clock for rate-limit headers or webhook cooldowns.

Only configure `background` if your runtime guarantees the task can finish. See [runtime guidance](/docs/embedding#other-fetch-based-runtimes).

## AppConfig

| Option      | Type                                                         | Required              | Default                                     | Behavior                                                        |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `provider`  | `Provider`                                                   | Yes                   | None                                        | Source of release metadata and assets                           |
| `adapters`  | `Adapter[]`                                                  | Yes                   | None                                        | Protocol routes mounted for this application                    |
| `authorize` | `(request: Request) => boolean` or `Promise<boolean>` result | For private providers | No access check                             | Denies with `401` when it returns false                         |
| `channels`  | `Record<string, (release: Release) => boolean>`              | No                    | Stable and prerelease predicates            | Replaces the default channel map                                |
| `cache`     | `CachePolicy`                                                | No                    | See below                                   | Sets this application's metadata lifetimes                      |
| `delivery`  | `"redirect"` or `"stream"`                                   | No                    | Redirect if public and provider supports it | Chooses public binary delivery; private providers always stream |

See [applications](/docs/configuration), [channels](/docs/channels) and [authentication](/docs/security) for examples.

## CachePolicy

| Option         | Type     | Required | Default      | Example                                             |
| -------------- | -------- | -------- | ------------ | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `ttl`          | `number` | No       | `60_000` ms  | `5 * 60 * 1000` for five minutes fresh              |
| `negativeTtl`  | `number` | No       | `15_000` ms  | `10 * 1000` for ten seconds with no releases        |
| `staleIfError` | `number` | No       | `300_000` ms | `10 * 60 * 1000` for ten extra minutes after expiry |

All values must be finite and nonnegative. Zero is allowed. A zero stale window disables serving old metadata after freshness ends. A zero TTL causes every check to need refresh coordination, so don't use it to bypass GitHub limits.

## Provider and adapter options

| Factory                    | Configuration reference                                                                           |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `github(options)`          | [GitHub options](/docs/github#options-you-may-need) and [test injection](/docs/api#githuboptions) |
| `tauri(options?)`          | [TauriOptions](/docs/api#taurioptions)                                                            |
| `electron(options?)`       | [ElectronOptions](/docs/api#electronoptions)                                                      |
| `android(options?)`        | [AndroidOptions](/docs/api#androidoptions)                                                        |
| `generic()`                | No options                                                                                        |
| `memoryCache(maxEntries?)` | [Memory cache](/docs/api#memorycache)                                                             |
| `sqliteCache(filename)`    | [SQLite cache](/docs/api#sqlitecache)                                                             |

The [CLI environment variables](/docs/deployment#environment-variables) configure the listener and configuration path. They aren't fields in `UpserveConfig`.


---
title: HTTP endpoints
description: Look up adapter routes, asset downloads, webhooks and CLI health checks.
---

Replace `APP` with your application ID and `CHANNEL` with a configured channel. If you've mounted Upserve under `/updates`, prefix every path below with `/updates`.

Applications with `authorize()` check it before adapter and asset routes. Webhooks use signature verification separately. For response bodies and statuses, follow the linked integration guide.

## Update protocols

| Adapter                    | Method    | Path                                        | Result                                  |
| -------------------------- | --------- | ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| [Tauri](/docs/tauri)       | GET       | `/APP/CHANNEL/tauri/latest.json`            | Static manifest or `204`                |
| Tauri                      | GET       | `/APP/CHANNEL/tauri/:target/:arch/:current` | Dynamic offer or `204`                  |
| [Electron](/docs/electron) | GET, HEAD | `/APP/CHANNEL/electron/:file`               | YAML or a matching history asset        |
| Electron                   | GET, HEAD | `/APP/CHANNEL/electron/:release/:file`      | Asset from an exact provider release ID |
| [Android](/docs/android)   | GET       | `/APP/CHANNEL/android/latest.json`          | Manifest or `204`                       |
| Android                    | GET       | `/APP/CHANNEL/android/update/:current`      | Newer eligible manifest or `204`        |
| [Generic](/docs/generic)   | GET       | `/APP/CHANNEL/generic/latest`               | Latest release or `204`                 |
| Generic                    | GET       | `/APP/CHANNEL/generic/update/:current`      | Newer release or `204`                  |
| Generic                    | GET       | `/APP/CHANNEL/generic/versions/:version`    | Exact version or `404`                  |
| Generic                    | GET       | `/APP/CHANNEL/generic/releases`             | `{ releases: [...] }`                   |
| Generic                    | GET       | `/APP/CHANNEL/generic/channels`             | `{ channels: [...] }`                   |

Current-version parameters are semantic versions, not tags. An unknown application or channel returns `404`. Generic channel discovery still requires a valid channel path, but doesn't fetch releases from GitHub.

## Asset downloads

`GET` and `HEAD /APP/CHANNEL/assets/:release/:asset` resolve a registered provider release ID and asset ID within the channel. Use URLs returned by the API instead of constructing them from filenames. Missing IDs return `404`.

The result redirects or streams according to the [delivery policy](/docs/assets). Range and conditional responses depend on the provider; the GitHub provider supports single ranges.

## Webhooks

`POST /webhooks/APP` is registered when the provider implements `verifyWebhook`. The GitHub provider requires a valid signature, a release event and the correct repository. See [webhooks](/docs/webhooks) for setup and status codes.

## Standalone health checks

The CLI adds these endpoints; `createUpserve()` alone doesn't:

| Path                | Response                                                                             |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `GET /health/live`  | `200`, `{ "status": "ok" }`                                                          |
| `GET /health/ready` | `200`, `{ "status": "ready" }`, or `503`, `{ "status": "draining" }` during shutdown |

These checks don't contact GitHub. Test an actual update endpoint to verify repository access and manifests.


---
title: Error responses
description: Interpret HTTP statuses and decide when an update client should retry.
---

An Upserve operational error returns a small JSON object, for example:

```json
{ "error": "network" }
```

Raw GitHub responses and credentials aren't sent to clients. Not every HTTP error has this JSON shape: unmatched routes and some missing assets use Hono's normal `404` response.

## Status codes

| Status                      | Meaning                                                                                 | What to do                                                                    |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `204 No Content`            | No release or applicable update for this request                                        | Keep the installed version; don't parse a JSON body                           |
| `304 Not Modified`          | Your metadata ETag still matches, or a download validator matched                       | Reuse your client-side cached response                                        |
| `401 Unauthorized`          | Application access denied, or webhook verification failed                               | Supply the correct downstream credentials or signature                        |
| `404 Not Found`             | Unknown route/channel, missing release, manifest or asset                               | Check the exact URL and selected release's assets                             |
| `422 Unprocessable Entity`  | Invalid version or upstream metadata                                                    | Correct the version or release files; repeated immediate retries won't fix it |
| `429 Too Many Requests`     | Valid webhook deliveries arrived inside the local cooldown                              | Redeliver later if needed                                                     |
| `503 Service Unavailable`   | Upstream failure, denied upstream access or refresh cooldown with no usable cached data | Respect `Retry-After` and investigate the error code                          |
| `500 Internal Server Error` | An unexpected error, including a plugin/storage exception                               | Inspect your server integration without logging secrets                       |

## Operational error codes

| JSON `error`    | Default HTTP status              | Meaning                                                                    |
| --------------- | -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `missing`       | `404`                            | A required resource isn't available                                        |
| `invalid`       | `422`                            | Metadata or version validation failed                                      |
| `auth`          | `503`                            | The upstream rejected access; this isn't a downstream client login failure |
| `network`       | `503`                            | An upstream request or manifest load failed                                |
| `rate_limit`    | `503`                            | Refresh is delayed; this may follow an earlier failure cooldown            |
| `configuration` | `503` if raised during a request | Invalid configuration; normally discovered at startup                      |
| `internal`      | `500`                            | An error outside the recognized operational categories                     |

The original failing request may report `auth` or `network`, while a later request during its cooldown reports `rate_limit`. An error code alone isn't a complete history of GitHub's response.

## Retry behavior

When an error carries a retry deadline, Upserve includes `Retry-After` as a number of seconds. Clients should wait at least that long and add their own jitter when many installations retry together. Don't add a force-refresh query or repeatedly invalidate metadata from clients.

A temporary failure can be hidden by a successful stale-data response until the configured stale window ends. A successful empty release list is different: it means there are no releases to offer. See [cache behavior](/docs/cache) and [symptom-based troubleshooting](/docs/troubleshooting).


---
title: Troubleshooting
description: Diagnose missing updates, upstream errors, private downloads and deployment problems.
---

Start with the exact endpoint your client uses. `curl -i` shows the status, body and `Retry-After` header. The CLI's readiness endpoint only checks the service lifecycle; it doesn't prove that GitHub access or update manifests work.

## My application doesn't detect a new release

1. Confirm the release is published, not a draft, and is in the channel your client requests.
2. Check `tagPrefix`. A tag `editor-v1.2.0` needs `tagPrefix: "editor-v"`; `1.2.0` needs an empty prefix.
3. If you've enabled the generic adapter, inspect selection directly:

```sh
curl -i http://localhost:3000/editor/stable/generic/latest
curl -i http://localhost:3000/editor/prerelease/generic/latest
```

The selected version must be newer than the client's version by semantic precedence. If the old release is still selected, wait for `ttl` or inspect your [release webhook](/docs/webhooks). Trusted embedded code can call `await updates.refresh("editor")`; clients can't force a refresh.

If selection is correct, inspect that framework's manifest in the **same release**. Upserve doesn't fall back to an older valid manifest when the newest release is incomplete.

## Upserve returns 204 even though a newer version exists

A `204` means the request has no applicable offer. It isn't an upstream error. Compare the selected channel, the current version in the URL, and any adapter compatibility rule.

For Tauri, check the exact `target-arch` platform key. For Android, inspect your `compatible()` hook; it can suppress even the latest-manifest endpoint. The default prerelease channel doesn't include stable releases. Use [custom channels](/docs/channels) if you want a different rule.

## My Tauri updater cannot find its platform

Request the static manifest:

```sh
curl -i http://localhost:3000/editor/stable/tauri/latest.json
```

Compare its `platforms` keys with the dynamic request. `/tauri/darwin/aarch64/1.0.0` looks up `darwin-aarch64`. A custom key won't match that convention; use the static endpoint and your client's custom-target support.

A `404` means `latest.json` is missing. A `422` means the manifest failed validation: check version, nonempty signatures and exact GitHub URLs for every platform. Keep the original signatures; changing the server endpoint doesn't require generating new ones.

## GitHub reports a rate-limit error

Look for `Retry-After` and wait. The provider respects primary and secondary rate limits. Existing metadata can still be served within its stale window, so an outage may not affect every check immediately.

Don't set TTLs to zero or clear the cache on every failure. If several service instances share one credential, their cooldowns aren't coordinated. Reduce the number of instances or budget upstream requests accordingly. For a public repository, you can authenticate API access with `token` and explicit `private: false`; never use that override for a private source.

## Upserve returns 503

Read the JSON `error`:

- `auth`: confirm the repository exists, the token can read it and the repository name is correct. GitHub can return `404` for a private repository you can't access; Upserve treats that as an access failure.
- `network`: check server egress to GitHub and download hosts, DNS and timeouts.
- `rate_limit`: honor the cooldown. This can follow an earlier network/access failure, not just a GitHub quota response.

If the cache is empty or its stale window has ended, Upserve can't answer from old data. Restoring upstream access is the fix. Increasing `staleIfError` only helps future outages when valid data has already been cached.

## Private release downloads return 401

A `401` on an application route means your `authorize()` callback denied the client. It isn't GitHub asking for its token. Send the **downstream** credential on both update checks and downloads:

```sh
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $UPDATE_CLIENT_TOKEN" \
  http://localhost:3000/editor/stable/generic/latest
```

Make sure your proxy forwards `Authorization` and your updater preserves the header for the server asset URL. A `503` with `auth` points to upstream repository access instead. See [authentication](/docs/security).

## Electron differential downloads fail

First fetch the platform YAML and verify it references files uploaded to that release. Keep old blockmaps available and set `useMultipleRangeRequest: false` in the generic provider configuration.

Test a returned installer URL through the same proxy your client uses:

```sh
curl -D - -H 'Range: bytes=0-1023' "$ASSET_URL" -o first-kib.bin
```

Expect `206` and `Content-Range` for a valid range. If the response is a redirect, repeat with `curl -L`. If the proxy changes it to a full `200`, inspect its range forwarding and buffering rules. Check the packaged client's logs too; full-download fallback, signing and installation are client behaviors.

## Large installers time out

The GitHub provider defaults to 30 seconds per upstream request. For streamed downloads, set `github({ repository: "owner/editor", timeout: 5 * 60 * 1000 })` and increase proxy/client timeouts as needed.

Public redirect delivery avoids streaming the full file through Upserve. Private assets must stream. A deployment shutdown has a separate ten-second CLI drain deadline, so a long transfer may be interrupted during restarts.

## SQLite cannot open its database

Use Node.js 22.13 or newer; Node.js 24 is recommended. Create the parent directory before calling `sqliteCache()`, and ensure the process can write there. The CLI creates `UPSERVE_CACHE_DIR` for you when it manages the store.

In Docker, the runtime user is UID/GID `10001`. Give that user write access to bind-mounted `/data`, or use the Compose named volume. Don't mount only the database file read-only; WAL needs writable adjacent files. See [SQLite setup](/docs/cache#persist-metadata-with-sqlite).

## Packages cannot be found on npm

During private initial development, publication may not have happened yet. Use the [checkout instructions](/docs/quick-start#run-from-a-repository-checkout). Don't replace the scoped package names with unrelated npm packages.
